cards.q: What is vSmart in Cisco SD-WAN?
cards.a: The control plane of Cisco SD-WAN. It runs OMP (Overlay Management Protocol) with all WAN edges, computes the overlay topology, and distributes centralized policy (routing, data, cflowd).
Running OMP as the control protocol, distributing edge routes, enforcing centralized policy, computing the topology, and managing SLA/app-aware paths — it is the brain of the overlay control plane.

cards.q: What does OMP carry between vSmart and the edges?
cards.a: OMP (overlay management protocol) carries routes and TLOCs between vSmart and the edges, with policy attached.

cards.q: What are the route types advertised in the OMP overlay?
cards.a: OMP routes (prefix/origin), TLOCs (transport location), service routes (VPN/ETR), and policy routes — routes are advertised as OMP routes with TLOCs.

cards.q: What is the SD-WAN policy model around vSmart?
cards.a: Centralized policy lives on vSmart and is pushed to edges; local policy is edge-based; app-route policy uses SLA; control policy does route filtering.

cards.q: Why use centralized control via vSmart?
cards.a: It provides one consistent policy source, agility in changing config centrally, scale because edges stay light, and global app-aware SLA — edges stay simple while vSmart does the thinking.

cards.q: What happens in SD-WAN if vSmart is down?
cards.a: No vSmart means no overlay control or policy, so the fabric loses control/routing intelligence.

cards.q: Which commands verify vSmart and OMP?
cards.a: show omp peers, show omp routes, show omp tlocs, show sdwan control, and show sdwan policy.

cards.q: OMP peers are not establishing with vSmart. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: vSmart being down or unreachable is likely; check show omp peers and show sdwan control.

cards.q: Routes are missing from the overlay. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A policy filter is likely; check show omp routes.

cards.q: No TLOCs are being advertised. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A transport issue is likely; check show omp tlocs.

cards.q: How do you distinguish vSmart from vBond and vManage?
cards.a: vBond opens the door (orchestration), vSmart steers (control plane + OMP + centralized policy), and vManage runs the GUI (management).
